title: Bowling ball versus ten pins

items.name: Long ramp
items.why: A long wooden ramp from 60 cm up down to the table, about 1.25 m long at about 29°

items.name: Bowling ball
items.why: The 7.26 kg ball waits at the top of the ramp until the release

items.name: Pin 1
items.why: First pin, hit by the ball

items.name: Pin 2
items.why: Pins stand 25 cm apart, closer than their 38 cm height, so each falls into the next

items.name: Pin 10
items.why: Last pin, its right edge about 9 cm from the table's end

notes: The ball's centre drops about 0.55 m down the ramp, so it reaches the table at about 2.8 m/s. It rolls 15 cm into the first pin and keeps ploughing down the row. Each falling pin (38 cm tall) also reaches the next one 25 cm away, so the whole row goes over within about 3 s.
assumptions: The pins stand in a single straight line left to right, not in the usual triangle, because all motion happens in one plane
Pins are spaced 25 cm apart (centre to centre) so the row fits on the table and each pin can topple the next
The ramp is 60 cm high at its top so the ball arrives fast enough to carry through the row
